subject: Animation
title: Squash and Stretch: The First Principle
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Squash and Stretch: The First Principle.

hook.text: Squash and stretch is the most important animation principle. Without it, objects look rigid and lifeless.

buildup.text: When a ball hits the ground, it squashes flat. When it bounces up, it stretches tall. This creates life.

discovery.text: Disney's animators discovered this by studying how real bodies deform during motion and impact.

twist.text: The volume must stay constant. If a ball gets wider, it must get shorter. Breaking this rule looks wrong.

climax.text: Squash and stretch applies to everything — faces, bodies, even dialogue. It is the heartbeat of animation.

punchline.text: The secret to animated life is knowing when to squash and when to stretch.

quiz.question: What rule must be maintained when applying squash and stretch?
options: The color must change with each deformation
The volume of the object must stay constant — wider means shorter, and vice versa
The object must return to its original shape immediately
